definition.rule: Mercenaries are hired soldiers who will guard, patrol, and campaign for anyone who pays their fee.
Unlike conscripts and militias, mercenaries must be found and recruited.

equipment_rules.rule: All mercenaries also carry a military tunic, cloak, pair of sandals, backpack, laborer’s tools, 4 stakes and mallet, mess kit, small tent, 2 wool blankets, and waterskin.
Cavalry mercenaries also carry saddle, bridle, 2 saddlebags, and grooming kit.
Missile-armed mercenaries carry 20 rounds of ammunition.

availability_in_markets.rule: Any character can hire mercenaries from markets.
Mercenaries recruited from a settlement are of the prevailing race of that settlement unless otherwise specified.
Dwarven troops and elven troops may only be found in dwarven and elven settlements.
Humanoid troops may only be found in Chaotic-aligned settlements.
Terrain and climate restrictions apply where listed.
Exotic troops are available only at Judge discretion.

crop_rules.rule: The total number available of a given type is called a crop.
One half of the crop, rounded up, becomes available within the first week after mustering begins.
Another quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, becomes available during the second week.
The remainder becomes available during the third week.
The market crop replenishes at the end of each month.

hiring_costs.rule: Each week spent finding mercenaries in a market requires a fee per mercenary type.

availability_in_realm.rule: A domain or realm leader, or a character acting with the leader’s permission, may recruit mercenaries from the entire realm.
Realm recruitment uses the same race, climate, and terrain restrictions as settlement recruitment.
Realm populations listed are minimum populations for their type; larger realms scale proportionately.

crop_rules.rule: One half of the realm crop, rounded up, becomes available in the first time period after mustering begins.
Another quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, becomes available in the second time period.
The remainder becomes available in the third time period.
The realm crop replenishes at the end of the fourth time period.

price_pressure.rule: If more than 50% of the crop of a mercenary type in a realm is hired, prices for that type throughout the realm increase by a percentage equal to the percentage over 50%.
Elevated prices remain even after a new crop appears until less than 50% of a crop is employed in the realm.

hiring_costs.rule: Each recruitment time period requires a fee per mercenary type.

hiring_procedure.rule: Availability does not guarantee service; mercenaries must still be recruited through negotiation.
For large-scale hiring, divide mercenaries into companies of 120, battalions of 500, or brigades of 2,000 when rolling on the Reaction to Hiring Offer table.
After hiring, mercenaries must be paid monthly wages by troop type and race.

morale_and_loyalty.rule: Mercenary morale is based on training and equipment, not employer magnetism.
Morale modifies both morale rolls and loyalty rolls.
Morale rolls are made during battles when casualties exceed an army’s break point.
A calamity is routing from battle, suffering 25% or greater casualties, being out of supply, or going without pay for a month.
When a calamity occurs, make a loyalty roll of 2d6 plus morale and adjustments.
If troops are suffering more than one calamity at once, apply -2 to the loyalty roll per calamity after the first.
Working conditions may modify morale upward or downward at Judge discretion.

outcome_definitions.entry: Troops immediately leave service; they may attack or stage a coup if the employer is vulnerable, or seek service with a strong enemy.
Troops leave service at the first advantageous safe moment and will not risk another battle or calamity.
Troops remain only because they see no better option; if rolled on two consecutive morale rolls they leave service.
Troops become dedicated servants; all future loyalty rolls are at +1; fanatic loyalty can never result from going without pay and becomes ordinary loyalty in that case.

veterans.rule: The average human mercenary is a 0th level normal man with 1-1 HD, attack throw 11+, and damage by weapon.
Veterans are generally 1st level fighters or explorers.
Veterans gain +1 morale over the base morale for their troop type.
Veterans cost an additional 12gp per month above the normal wage for their type.
Up to 25% of human mercenaries hired may be veterans.
Elven and dwarven mercenaries are already equivalent to veterans.

exotic_mercenaries.rule: Exotic mercenaries may include trained animals, constructs, or fantastic creatures.
To determine available quantity, use the Exotic row of the mercenary availability table and divide by the creature’s total monthly cost on the Exotic Creatures Roster.
Total monthly cost includes wages, supplies, and specialists needed to handle the creature.
Exotic mercenaries use the normal mercenary finding and hiring rules, but the finding cost is multiplied by exotic type.
The Judge may adjust availability and cost by setting.

definition.rule: A domain leader can permanently conscript peasants into an army.
Up to 1 conscript per 10 peasant families may be levied without affecting domain morale or revenue.
Conscription may be done all at once or gradually.
If peasant families decrease, some conscripts must be released.
If peasant families increase, more conscripts may be levied.
If conscripts are killed, they can only be replaced through population growth.

untrained_state.rule: Untrained conscripts have no weapons or armor, 1d4 hit points, morale -2, and fight as normal men.
Unless trained, they may only use spears, clubs, quarterstaffs, or daggers.

training.rule: Conscripts may be trained into the same troop varieties as mercenaries.
Eligibility by troop type is limited by aptitude and race.
Trained conscripts gain the same characteristics as mercenaries of their type.
Trained conscripts must be paid the wages appropriate to their troop type.

eligibility_rules_human.rule: Any able-bodied conscript can qualify as light infantry.
50% qualify as slingers, bowmen, or crossbowmen.
Two-thirds of those who qualify as light cavalry, 17% of total conscripts, qualify as medium cavalry.
25% qualify as longbowmen because they must qualify as both heavy infantry and bowmen.
12.5% qualify as horse archers because they must qualify as both bowmen and cavalry.
8.5% qualify as heavy cavalry because they must qualify as both heavy infantry and medium cavalry.
5% qualify as cataphract cavalry because they must qualify as heavy infantry, bowmen, and medium cavalry.

morale.rule: Newly levied conscripts have base morale -2.
After training, base morale becomes that of the trained troop type.
Conscripts from domains with Steadfast or Stalwart morale gain a one-time +1 morale increase.
Conscripts from domains with Apathetic or Demoralized morale suffer a one-time -1 morale penalty.
Working conditions may further modify morale.
Conscripts make morale rolls during battles when casualties exceed break point.
Conscripts make loyalty rolls when suffering any calamity.
Use the Unit Loyalty table for loyalty results.
Conscripts cannot voluntarily leave service; loyalty results that would cause departure represent desertion.
If released by their leader, trained conscripts become mercenaries or brigands, while untrained conscripts return to their farms.

notes.rule: Marshal cost is per troop, assuming each marshal trains 60 troops.

definition.rule: A domain leader may levy a peasant militia in addition to conscripts.
Up to 2 additional peasants per 10 families may be levied.
For each peasant levied, domain revenue is reduced by one family.
Levying 1 or fewer militia per 10 families reduces domain morale by 1; levying 2 per 10 families reduces domain morale by 2.
These penalties remain until the militia is sent home.
If militia are killed, the loss of domain morale and family revenue is permanent.

untrained_state.rule: Untrained militia have no weapons or armor, 1d4 hit points, fight as normal men, and have morale -2.
Militia cost 3gp per month while called up, or more if trained.

training.rule: Militia may be trained like conscripts and use the same training qualification logic and training cost table.
If trained and then sent home, militia keep their equipment.
When called up again, trained militia return with that equipment and fight as the trained troop type.
Trained militia use the same characteristics as mercenaries of their type and are paid the wages for that type while called up.
Militia are assumed to pass arms and skills to their heirs when no longer capable of serving.

risk_rule.rule: If domain morale becomes Turbulent, Defiant, or Rebellious, any rebels are drawn from the militia.

morale.rule: New militia have base morale -2.
Trained militia have the base morale of their troop type.
Militia from domains with Steadfast or Stalwart morale gain a one-time +1 morale bonus.
Militia from domains with Apathetic or Demoralized morale suffer a one-time -1 morale penalty.
Working conditions may further modify morale.
Militia make morale rolls during battle when casualties exceed break point.
Militia make loyalty rolls when they suffer a calamity.
Militia also treat each season of continuous campaigning as a calamity.
Use the Unit Loyalty table for loyalty results.
Militia cannot voluntarily leave service, but may desert, betray, or attack their leader.
If voluntarily released, militia return to their farms.

definition.rule: A domain leader may have followers available for army service.
Follower arms and equipment are determined by class-based follower tables.

morale.rule: Follower base morale equals that of a mercenary of the same troop type.
Followers add the leader’s Charisma bonus to morale, to a maximum of +4.
Working conditions may further modify morale.
Followers make morale rolls during battle when casualties exceed break point.
Followers make loyalty rolls when suffering a calamity.
For followers, a calamity is routing from battle, suffering 25% or greater casualties, being out of supply, or going without pay for a month.

religious_fanatics.rule: Cleric and bladedancer followers are religious fanatics.
Religious fanatics need only basic upkeep of 3gp per month.
Religious fanatics always have Base Morale +4 regardless of equipment.
Religious fanatics do not make loyalty rolls for calamities, but still make morale rolls in battle.

follower_table_notes.rule: Hunters are treated as Light Infantry for wages and morale.
Composite Bowmen are treated as Longbowmen for wages and morale.
Gnomish Tricksters replace dwarven troops with gnomish troops of the same type.

definition.rule: Whether a realm uses slave soldiers is at Judge discretion.

availability.rule: Use the mercenary availability tables to determine slave soldier availability.
Slave soldiers displace 10% to 90% of mercenaries available in a market or realm, depending on how widespread they are.
Slave soldiers need not match the prevailing race of the realm or settlement.

buying.rule: Finding and buying slave soldiers uses the same time requirements and gp search costs as recruiting mercenaries.
Instead of wages, slave soldiers are purchased at a variable cost by race, training, and equipment.
Once obtained, slave soldiers cost 3gp per month in upkeep; cavalry and ogres cost 16gp per month in upkeep.
Failure to pay upkeep counts as a calamity for morale purposes.
Supplemental pay, better food, and other privileges may improve morale over time.
At Judge discretion, slave soldiers may be hired from an owner instead of purchased outright; in that case their monthly cost equals the normal wage for their troop type and is paid to the owner.

training.rule: Leaders may conscript, capture, or purchase suitable youths and train them into slave soldiers.
Suitable candidates must be able-bodied and no older than Youth age category for their race.
In Chaotic societies, one suitable candidate per 10 peasant families may be enslaved without affecting morale or revenue.
Enslaving more candidates has the same morale and revenue penalties as levying militia.
Enslaving families in Lawful or Neutral realms is not permitted; doing so changes realm alignment.
25% of prisoners taken while pillaging a domain are suitable to become slave soldiers.
Market-bought candidates cost 40gp each.
If the market does not have enough candidates, more may be commissioned; this takes 40 days at 1 day per gp.
Indoctrination lasts 5 years.
Indoctrination costs 180gp in upkeep per candidate.
One marshal is required per 60 candidates at 30gp per month.
After indoctrination, slave soldiers are trained into troop types using the conscript training rules.

exotic_slaves.rule: Purchase prices listed for creatures are for tamed and trained creatures.
Exotic slaves do not require wages, but still require supplies and specialists.
Sentient exotics are reliable only if captured young and raised in captivity.
Adult sentient exotics make a loyalty roll whenever they have an opportunity to escape or betray their master.
Apply the creature’s normal morale bonus as a penalty to such loyalty rolls.
Exotic slaves are generally very rare and always Judge-controlled in availability.

morale.rule: Slave soldiers enslaved as adults have morale -4.
Slave soldiers enslaved as children have the same morale as normal mercenaries of their type.
Child-raised slave soldiers gain a permanent +1 morale bonus while serving the leader who trained them.
This +1 bonus is lost if they are sold or hired out.
Slave soldiers make loyalty rolls as conscripts.
Like conscripts, they cannot voluntarily leave service, but may desert, betray, or attack their leader.

mother_of_dragons_memorial_rule.rule: If freed, slave soldiers immediately make a loyalty roll modified by the liberator’s Charisma.
If the result is Fanatic Loyalty, they become liberator-worshipping fanatics, need only 3gp per month upkeep, and have Base Morale +4 regardless of equipment.

definition.rule: A realm leader cannot directly access the troops employed by vassals without a call to arms.
On a call to arms, a vassal must muster at least half the garrison of the vassal’s realm.
Demanding the full garrison counts as demanding two duties and may provoke a Henchman Morale roll unless offset by a boon.
Calls to arms are based on the garrison of the vassal’s realm, not the vassal’s personal domain.
Each vassal is responsible for issuing calls to sub-vassals in turn.
A domain garrison is some mix of followers, mercenaries, conscripts, and militia.

realm_size_rules.rule: The Vassal Troops by Realm Size table estimates available troops for different realm sizes.
The table assumes garrison expenditures of 2gp per peasant family each month.
Borderlands and wilderness domains may have more troops.
Highly militarized or total-war realms may have garrisons 50% to 100% larger than listed.
Leaders usually do not muster the maximum because of morale pressure, gifts required, supply burden, and the need to retain reserves.

time_required.rule: When a call to arms is issued, one half of the requested troops, rounded up, arrives in the first time period.
Another quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, arrives in the second time period.
The remainder arrives in the third time period.
Troops generally muster at the realm leader’s stronghold unless ordered elsewhere.
Geography, dispersion, or enemy isolation may prevent a single rendezvous point; the Judge determines actual muster points.

standing_armies.rule: A realm leader may maintain a standing army instead of relying on vassal troops.
A standing army usually requires a special tax on vassals of 1gp or more per peasant family.
Each gp taxed counts as demanding a duty.
Taxes of 2gp or more may provoke Henchman Morale rolls just like calling up troops.
Standing armies are usually distributed across the realm to supplement local garrisons.
Leaders relying on vassals usually field conscripts from domains; leaders relying on standing armies usually hire mercenaries.

definition.rule: After troops are raised, they must be organized into units and divisions and assigned officers.

units.rule: A unit may contain up to 120 man-sized creatures, 60 large creatures, 20 huge creatures, 5 gigantic creatures, or 1 colossal creature.
Where possible, units should be homogeneous by race, class, level, Hit Dice, and equipment.
Mixed units are allowed if necessary.
Every unit has a minimum equivalent of 20 men and maximum equivalent of 120 men.
units.restriction: Living and undead creatures may not be in the same unit.
Infantry and cavalry may not be in the same unit.

divisions.rule: After units are created, units are assigned to divisions.
A division is a group of nearby units under a commander reporting to the army leader.
An army must have at least 3 units.
Maximum divisions equals the maximum number of henchmen the army leader may retain: 4 plus Charisma modifier.
If the army leader has Leadership proficiency, increase maximum divisions by 1.

leadership_ability.rule: Leadership ability is the maximum number of units a character can readily control in battle.
Leadership ability also determines the maximum number of divisions the leader may have.
For characters, leadership ability equals 4 plus Charisma modifier.
For monstrous officers without Charisma scores, leadership ability is 3 + 1 per 4 HD, rounded down, maximum 8.

officers.rule: Each division must have a commander.
Each unit may have a lieutenant, but one is not required.
The army leader usually serves as one commander.
Other commanders are usually adventurers, henchmen, followers, or hired mercenary officers.

qualifications.rule: PCs and NPCs must be at least 7th level to serve as commanders in campaign battle and at least 5th level to serve as lieutenants.
Monsters must have at least 4 more HD than the average of creatures they command to serve as commanders and at least 2 more HD than average to serve as lieutenants.
A beastman chieftain can always command company-sized units of its own race regardless of HD.
A beastman sub-chieftain can always serve as lieutenant for a company-sized unit of its race regardless of HD.
The Judge may waive officer requirements if circumstances justify command.

strategic_ability.rule: Strategic ability equals the better bonus from Intelligence or Wisdom, minimum 0, minus the worse penalty from Intelligence or Wisdom, maximum 0.
Each rank of Military Strategy proficiency adds +1.
Minimum strategic ability is -3 and maximum is +6.
For monstrous officers without Intelligence or Wisdom, strategic ability is 0 + 1 per 5 HD, rounded down.
Sub-human intelligence reduces monstrous strategic ability by 1.
Generally high intelligence increases it by 1.
The Judge may adjust monstrous strategic ability for experience and tactical knowledge.

morale_modifier.rule: Morale modifier affects Unit Morale rolls for units under the officer’s command; it does not affect Unit Loyalty rolls.
Morale modifier equals Charisma bonus or penalty.
Barbarians, bards, explorers, fighters, and paladins of 5th level or higher gain +1 morale modifier.
Legendary leader status adds +1 morale modifier.
Monsters without Charisma usually have morale modifier 0.
If a monster entry states that monsters of a type gain a morale bonus while that commander lives, use that bonus as the commander’s morale modifier.

role_of_officers.rule: Leadership ability, strategic ability, and morale modifier materially affect army performance.
Armies with mediocre officers or too few officers are substantially disadvantaged.

small_and_large_armies.rule: Armies of 600 to 3,000 troops use the standard company and division structure.
Armies of 600 or fewer troops use platoon-scale units.
Armies of 3,001 to 12,000 troops use battalion-scale units.
Armies of 12,001 or more troops use brigade-scale units.
Smaller units allow lower-level officers to matter individually.

beastmen_officers.rule: A beastman sub-chieftain can always serve as commander or lieutenant of a platoon-scale unit of its race regardless of HD.
At battalion and brigade scale, beastmen get no special officer advantage.

rump_troops.rule: If excess troops are less than half a unit, ignore them as reserves, trainees, or sick troops.
If excess troops are at least half a unit, organize them as one or more understrength units.
For large-scale units, sizes may be rounded to the nearest 500 infantry per battalion or 2,000 infantry per brigade to reduce rump troops.

definition.rule: Armies require specialists in addition to troops and officers.
Player characters with appropriate proficiencies may act as specialists where noted.
The list of specialists is not exhaustive.

artillerist.rule: Required to employ siege artillery such as ballistae, catapults, and trebuchets.
One artillerist can oversee a battery of 3 to 5 artillery pieces.

armorer.rule: An armorer can make 40gp worth of weapons, armor, or shields each month.
Armies require 1 armorer per 60 troops, equal to 2 per standard unit, to maintain and repair weapons and armor.
An armorer may be assisted by up to 2 journeymen at 20gp/month each and 4 apprentices at 10gp/month each.
An armorer with 1 journeyman and 2 apprentices produces 100gp/month and can maintain 150 troops.
An armorer with 2 journeymen and 4 apprentices produces 160gp/month and can maintain 240 troops.
If no armorer is provided, troops maintain their own gear and the unit suffers -1 morale until an armorer is provided.

creature_handler.rule: A creature handler is trained to safely handle hunting or guard creatures in battle conditions.
One handler is required per 6 hunting creatures or 20 guard creatures in battlefield conditions.
No handler is required for mounts or war mounts under rider control.
Trained animals used for ordinary non-battle purposes do not require handlers.
If a creature is gigantic or larger, handlers cost at least 150gp/month.

marshal.rule: Marshals train soldiers in discipline, fitness, and weapon drill.
Minimum requirement is 1 marshal per 60 troops being trained.

mercenary_officer.rule: Mercenary officers may serve as lieutenants or division commanders.
Typical officer class distribution in ordinary settlements: fighters 60%, anti-paladins 3%, barbarians 10%, bards 10%, explorers 10%, paladins 5%, ruinguards 2%.
Typical officer class distribution in elven settlements: courtiers 30%, rangers 40%, spellswords 30%.
Typical officer class distribution in dwarven settlements: delvers 10%, furies 10%, vaultguards 80%.
Roll 3d6 for the officer’s Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma.
For colonels and generals, one ability score may be re-rolled and the new result used if desired.
Apply normal officer characteristic rules to convert ability scores into leadership, strategic ability, and morale modifier.
All mercenary officers have base morale -2 because of inherent disloyalty.
Mercenary officers make morale rolls whenever they suffer a calamity.
Mercenary officers also make morale rolls whenever offered a higher wage by another employer.
If mercenary officers betray their leader, they take any units assigned to their command.

quartermaster.rule: Quartermasters manage supply distribution to a unit.
Armies require 1 quartermaster per unit to efficiently maintain supply lines.
A unit without a quartermaster has doubled supply cost and -1 morale until one is provided.

siege_engineer.rule: Siege engineers build and place temporary defensive works and construct and operate war machines and siege devices.

availability_in_markets.rule: Any character may hire military specialists from markets.
Some specialist entries use percentage chances for presence.
One half of available specialists, rounded up, becomes available in the first week.
Another quarter, rounded down with minimum 1, becomes available in the second week.
The remainder becomes available in the third week.
Market availability replenishes at the end of each month.
Finding fees are identical to mercenary search fees.
